title: Short Stuff: Devil Horns
summary: Short Stuff episode on the origin of the devil horns hand sign, part of a metal two-parter. Josh and Chuck explain that the sign is called the "corna," an Italian gesture for horns used to ward off the evil eye, and that it is often misattributed to Ronnie James Dio, who said in a 2001 interview he was not the originator. Gene Simmons tried to trademark a similar sign (with the thumb extended, resembling the ASL "I love you"). Geezer Butler claimed Black Sabbath used it first, which the hosts dispute. The hosts credit Jinx Dawson, lead singer of the Chicago occult rock band Coven, whose 1969 album Witchcraft Destroys Minds & Reaps Souls shows the sign on its back cover. They note Coven's bassist Greg "Oz" Osbourne and the simultaneous Black Sabbath name change, and that Lester Bangs compared Black Sabbath to Cream and Coven. They also mention the Japanese fox sign used at metal shows. The episode closes with updates to their top metal bands lists and a tribute to Ozzy Osbourne.
topics: Witchcraft Destroys Minds and Reaped Souls

segments.title: Opening banter
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck introduce the short stuff on devil horns as part of a metal two-parter, and Chuck mentions practicing the sign before a Judas Priest pre-show.

segments.title: Meaning of the corna gesture
segments.summary: Chuck explains the sign's Italian origin as the corna, used to ward off the evil eye, which is the opposite of a Satanic salute. Josh introduces Ronnie James Dio as the name most often credited, since he needed a signature gesture after Ozzy Osbourne left Black Sabbath.

segments.title: Other metal hand signals and Dio's disclaimer
segments.summary: The hosts discuss Van Halen and Sammy Hagar's hand signal and other bands' gestures. Chuck notes Dio said in a 2001 interview he was not the originator.

segments.title: Gene Simmons trademark attempt
segments.summary: Josh describes Gene Simmons trying to trademark a devil-horns-like sign with the thumb extended, which resembles the ASL I love you sign, and says the controversy surfaced the real early users.
topics: American Sign Language I love you sign

segments.title: Geezer Butler's claim
segments.summary: Chuck mentions Geezer Butler's claim that he flashed the sign in a 1969 photo and suggested it to Dio, and a Yellow Submarine cover image. The hosts say Butler is also wrong.

segments.title: Coven and Jinx Dawson
segments.summary: Josh credits Jinx Dawson, lead singer of the Chicago occult rock band Coven, as probably the first to use the sign. They discuss the 1969 album Witchcraft Destroys Minds and Reaped Souls, its song titles, and the back cover showing the gesture, and Dawson's Left Hand Path upbringing.
topics: Witchcraft Destroys Minds and Reaped Souls

segments.title: Black Sabbath and Coven connection
segments.summary: The hosts note Coven bassist Greg Oz Osbourne and that Black Sabbath changed its name at the same time. Black Sabbath denies hearing Coven, and Lester Bangs compared Black Sabbath to Cream and Coven.

segments.title: Japanese fox sign
segments.summary: Josh describes the kitsune fox hand sign used at Japanese metal shows, including by Babymetal, formed with the ring and middle fingers meeting the thumb while the index and pinky extend.

segments.title: Band list update and Ozzy tribute
segments.summary: Chuck updates his top five metal bands, swapping Scorpions for Tesla. Josh mentions clips of Ozzy Osbourne's funeral and his final performance of Coming Home in Birmingham.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck pay tribute to Ozzy Osbourne and close the short stuff.
